Recommendations of Experts
Committee on marketing strategy by
KVIC
*61. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the
Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that
recommendations of Experts Committee to
strengthen marketing strategy were not acted
upon by the KVIC;
(b) whether trading units having an
investment of Rs. 89.57 crores were running
in losses; and
(c) if so, the action proposed to be taken
against the CEO and CAO of KVIC for not
implementing the said recommendations?
Statutory dues of CPSUs employees
*62. SHRIMATI CHANDRA
KALA PANDEY:
SHRI DIPANKAR
MUKHERJEE:
Will the Minister of LABOUR be pleased
to refer to the reply to Starred Question 63
given in the Rajya Sabha on the
23rd November, 2000, and state:
(a) the status of statutory dues payable
to the employees of CPSUs;
(b) the amount liquidated so far;
(c) the status of present dues against
P.F., gratuity vis-a-vis status on
the 23rd November, 2000, enterprise-
wise;
(d) whether employees of Burn
Standard, National Instruments, Bharat
Brakes and Valves are not being paid wages
for the last 4-5 months; and
(e) if so, the action taken by
Government to pay the arrears of wages
immediately?
WLL service in Karnataka
*63. SHRI K.C. KONDAIAH: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
launch Wireless Local Loop (WLL) service
by the Department of Telecommunications
in Karnataka; and
(b) if so, the details of the cities proposed
to be covered under WLL service?

Regularisation of contract labourers
*64. SHRI S. VIDUTHALAI
VIRUMBI: Will the Minister of LABOUR
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Supreme
Court has recently ruled that the workers
(contract labourers) would not be
automatically absorbed as regular
employees; and
(b) if so, what action has been taken or
is proposed to be taken to protect the interests
of the contract workers?
Fishermen held in Sri Lanka
†*65. DR. A.K. PATEL: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian
fishermen were held for fishing in
Sri Lankan waters;
(b) if so, the number thereof; and
(c) the steps Government have taken so
far to get them released?
Cost overrun by Central sector
projects
*66. SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:
SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that an analysis by
the Associated Chambers of Commerce and
Industry of India (ASSOCHAM) has
revealed that as many as 466 Central sector
projects in different States suffer cost
overrun by about 36 per cent;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that ASSOCHAM
has made some suggestions to help reduce
the cost overrun; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and
Government's reaction thereto?
Restructuring of KVIC
†*67. SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: Will the
Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Khadi and
Village Industries Commission has decided
to shift from conventional industries of the
country and encourage setting-up of new
industries to keep pace with the
modernisation in the era of globalization;
(b) if so, the details of the decision taken
in this regard; and
(c) the changes proposed by the
Commission in the existing structure of
village industries in the light of the said
decision?
Cut-off of Indian news for the Indian
High Commission in Islamabad
*68. DR. Y. LAKSHMI PRASAD:
SHRI YADLAPATI VENKAT
RAO:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Pakistan has cut-off Indian
news for the Indian High Commission in
Islamabad;
(b) if so, the protest made for
infringement of the right to information; and
(c) the Pakistan Government's response
thereto?
Uranium dust in the Nuclear Fuel
Complex, Hyderabad
*69. DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:

Fuel Complex, Hyderabad, air is thick with

(c) if so, what preventive measures have
been taken by Government to avoid health

Unsold stocks of KVIC
439. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the
Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that KVIC
continued to incur huge losses due to
unsold stocks and lack of credit policies;
(b) whether unsold stocks increased
from 30.96 crore in 1994-95 to 49.02 crore
by the end of March, 2000;
(c) whether KVIC was not able to
furnish age/item-wise break-up of closing
stocks; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the
action proposed to be taken against the
officers of KVIC for this mess?
Misuse of funds by KVIC
440. SHRI ABANI ROY: Will the
Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that KVIC is
habitual in misusing Government funds;
(b) whether administrative expenditure
exceeded the sanctioned amount by 118
per cent;
(c) whether KVIC diverted Rs. 135.21
crore from Plan to Non-Plan funds without
Governments prior approval; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Mining rights along coastal area of
Kerala
441. SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any applications from private companies
through the State Government of Kerala
seeking approval for getting lease for
mining right to mine the mineral resources
along the coastal area of Kerala;
(b) if so, the number of such
applications and the details of such private
companies;
(c) whether Government have taken
any decision on the applications;
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not
the action proposed to be taken on the
same; and
(e) Governments reaction to lease out
the coastal area having immense mineral
wealth of strategic importance to private
companies for mining operations?

97
WIN2\SESSION\3356RS1 97
Rare earth mineral deposits in Kerala
442. SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) what is the expected quantity of rare
earth mineral deposits in the coastal area
of Kollam and Alleppey Districts of Kerala;
(b) whether Government have conducted
any study in this regard;
(c) if so, the findings thereof;
(d) whether Government have received
any applications seeking order for high level
probe into the alleged move of leasing out
the mining rights to a particles company;
(e) if so, the action taken in the matter
and details thereof; and
(f) if not, the action proposed to be taken
in the mater?
Improvement of facilities by Nuclear
Fuel Corporation
443. SHRI C.P. THIRUNAVUK-
KARASU: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Nuclear Fuel
Corporation has drawn a strategy to
improve its facilities to meet the increasing
demand;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the Department of Atomic
Energy has set up a target of 20,000 M.W.
power generation by 2020; and
(d) if so, the measures taken to achieve
the target?
Security measures in and around nuclear
installations
444. SHRI DINA NATH MISHRA:
SHRI RAMA SHANKER
KAUSHIK:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
high security measures in and around the
nuclear installations in the country in
view of the International Atomic Energy
Agency’s alert call about the potential
nuclear terrorism;
(b) whether there have been cases of
theft or trafficking of nuclear materials
and radio active resources in the country
during past five years; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Mobile phone subscribers
445. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of Mobile Phones
Subscribers as on the September, 2001
and their number in the five metro cities
of Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bangalore
and Kolkata;
(b) the number of cellular operators
and their names in the above cities; and
(c) the growth rate of subscribers
base in the first six months of the current
financial year?
MTNL-Broadcasters tie up
446. DR. Y. LAKSHMI PRASAD:
Will the Minister of COM-
MUNICATIONS be pleased to state:
(a) whether MTNL propose to tie up
with broadcasters for entering the cable
television segment;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the advantage of convergence
with the Prasar Bharati in this regard?
